page: OVHcloud r3-64 is a memory-optimized server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores from the AMD EPYC processor family running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, with one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is equipped with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 3078.58 in stress-ng tests, which places it in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 24583.04 and a PassMark CPU score of 20449.24. Memory performance is a key highlight, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and a strong large-block write bandwidth of 101.05 GB/sec. Large-block read bandwidth is average at 172.7 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates strong text generation speeds of 293.38 tokens per second using a small 135M LLM, while medium 7B model inference remains average.

The r3-64 instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads due to its dedicated core allocation and high RAM density. However, because it lacks hyperthreading and has a moderate base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, it may not be optimal for compute-bound parallel processing tasks that require dense thread counts. The combination of 64 GB of RAM, dedicated AMD EPYC cores, and local NVMe storage makes this instance highly suitable for memory-optimized databases, caching layers like Redis, and moderate-scale data processing tasks.
